stem: A gaming leaderboard company's platform team needs an in-memory cache for player rank data that must survive an instance restart and fail over automatically to a replica with no manual intervention.

choices.text: Amazon CloudFront configured to cache the leaderboard API responses at edge locations
Amazon ElastiCache for Redis OSS, with persistence and automatic failover enabled
An API Gateway stage cache in front of the leaderboard endpoint

rationale: Amazon ElastiCache for Redis OSS adds persistence through snapshots and append-only files plus replication with Multi-AZ automatic failover, which is exactly what a cache that must survive a restart and fail over on its own needs. Memcached is a simpler, multithreaded pure cache with no persistence and no replication, so an instance loss or restart loses the cached rank data outright. CloudFront caches whole HTTP responses at the edge to reduce origin load; it does not give the leaderboard service itself a durable, failover-capable in-memory data store. An API Gateway stage cache only caches responses for a single API stage to reduce backend calls; like CloudFront, it does not provide the durable, replicated cache the scenario asks for.
